mints_method: Token set chosen on 2026-11-07 by USD value of each token's supply on Solana. Universe: the 4,137 tokens on Jupiter's verified list (lite-api.jup.ag/tokens/v2/tag?query=verified), with DefiLlama's per-chain stablecoin supply (stablecoins.llama.fi) as a cross-check for stablecoins. Value = on-chain mint supply (getTokenSupply on mainnet, slots 466338590 to 466339188) times the Jupiter Price API v3 USD price, read at 2026-11-07T02:10:12Z and rounded to $0.1M. Prices agree with CoinGecko within 0.7%, except dSOL, where CoinGecko was 14% above the on-chain stake-pool exchange rate (1.2236 SOL per dSOL); Jupiter matches the pool rate. Excluded before ranking: wSOL (native SOL wrapper, no authority); tokenized securities such as xStocks equities and tokenized funds like BUIDL (they fit none of the four kinds, and Jupiter prices for thinly traded xStocks are often stale); pool and vault receipt tokens backed by other SPL tokens (JLP, jlUSDC, PST, syrupUSDC), which would count value already in the set twice and whose controls sit in programs; and tokens whose quoted value cannot be realized (GOHOME: about 5% of supply circulating and $0.3M of liquidity behind a $749M paper value; tSAT). Within each kind, tokens were ranked by value and the census keeps the top 7 stablecoins, the top 5 liquid-staking tokens, the top 3 wrapped or bridged assets and the top 7 Solana-native tokens: 22 tokens worth about $29.5B together. Next in line: SoFiUSD ($266M), mSOL ($204M), Wormhole WETH ($96M), PENGU ($503M). Each mint was checked against an issuer or operator page (source_url) and also matches CoinGecko's Solana contract field and Jupiter's verified flag; fwdSOL is not on CoinGecko and is confirmed by Sanctum, which runs its pool; Omni Bridge ZEC has no issuer page listing it, so it rests on Jupiter's verified flag plus CoinGecko's contract field. Values use the full mint supply, so for USDT and USDC they include balances still held by the issuer; DefiLlama's circulating figures on Solana are lower (USDT $2.44B, USDC $7.02B).

programs_method: Protocol set: the 25 largest protocols by Solana-chain TVL on DefiLlama. Source: https://api.llama.fi/protocols read at 2026-11-07T02:15:35Z, using chainTvls.Solana (the Solana entry only; borrowed, staking and pool2 keys are not added). Merging: child listings that share a DefiLlama parentProtocol are merged into one protocol. For a merged protocol the TVL is DefiLlama's own parent figure, currentChainTvls.Solana from https://api.llama.fi/protocol/<parent slug>, read at the time given in tvl_read_at; that figure drops the tokens DefiLlama lists under tokensExcludedFromParent (tokens one child holds that another child of the same parent already counts, such as JupSOL, JLP and JupUSD deposited in Jupiter Lend), so they are counted once. The children and their own figures are kept in defillama_children, and category is the category of the largest child. Exclusions: every CEX listing (category CEX) is dropped because it is exchange custody, not an on-chain program; 10 of them would otherwise be in the top 25: Binance CEX $6.34B; Bybit $864.2M; Bitget $862.5M; MEXC $740.2M; OKX $703.0M; Backpack $445.2M; Gate $403.1M; KuCoin $263.7M; Bitfinex $163.1M; BingX $91.7M. Chain-level entries (categories Chain and Canonical Bridge) are dropped too; none was near the cut (largest: NEAR Bridge $6.1M). Exchange-issued liquid staking tokens (BNSOL, bbSOL) are on-chain stake pools, not CEX listings, and stay in. Risk curators stay in and are marked as having no own program. Cut-off: #25 is Helius Staked SOL at $87.1M; next are RockawayX $85.3M, BlazeStake $78.8M, Unit $78.2M. Program ids: for each protocol, the mainnet program(s) that hold user funds or can move them (pools, vaults, lending markets, stake-pool programs, bridge token pools, routers and off-ramps that move user tokens). Left out: oracles and pricing programs, fee and rate-model programs, governance programs, swap routers that do not custody funds, devnet and staging ids. Every id but one comes from an official source (the protocol's docs, its official GitHub declare_id! or config, or its official SDK), cited in source_url. Those ids were checked on mainnet with getAccountInfo between 2026-11-07T02:16:03Z and 2026-11-07T02:16:42Z: each is an executable account owned by the upgradeable BPF loader. The exception, added after an independent check found it missing: Orca's legacy token-swap v1 program DjVE6JNiYqPL2QXyCUUh8rNjHrbz9hXHNYt99MQ59qw1, which DefiLlama's Orca adapter counts in Orca's Solana TVL (source_url points to that adapter). It is an executable account owned by BPFLoader2111111111111111111111111111111111, so it is immutable (checked 2026-11-07T08:41Z, slot 466,448,726). Protocols that run only on programs operated by someone else (for example LSTs on the SPL Stake Pool or Sanctum programs, or curators) have own_program false and an empty program_ids; the shared programs they use are in uses_programs, with the pool account whose owner program was checked on-chain at the same time. Known overlaps, left as DefiLlama reports them: DefiLlama's Sanctum Validator LSTs figure includes the separately listed JupSOL, fwdSOL, dSOL, dfdvSOL, bbSOL, hSOL and phaseSOL pools (together $1.41B); without them Sanctum would be about $415.4M and still in the top 25. Sentora's whole figure is curated deposits that are also counted inside Kamino and Jupiter.

programs.notes: DefiLlama's Sanctum Validator LSTs adapter sums every pool owned by the SanctumSpl and SanctumSplMulti programs (minus what sits in Infinity). That includes pools DefiLlama also lists as separate protocols: JupSOL, fwdSOL, dSOL, dfdvSOL, bbSOL, hSOL and phaseSOL (pool owners verified on-chain).
